automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Only a source with a visible publication or update timestamp strictly inside this UTC interval qualifies. Date-only records were used only when their calendar date was unambiguously inside the interval; boundary-only, missing, ambiguous, and future dates were excluded.

source_method: Public-web collection using NVD's public CVE API, linked vendor and maintainer advisories, public upstream commits/releases, and federation-index checks. No private or local repository content was sent externally.
searched_topics: agent and tool security including MCP, plugins, browsers, delegated authority, and autonomous action
identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
threat modeling, red teaming, security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates
AI security standards, regulation, governance, audit evidence, and risk management
public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned

qualifying_findings.title: Pydantic AI Harness ANSI stripping can block agent runs
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record with the linked upstream GitHub security advisory; NVD records CVSS 7.5 High.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Applications using pydantic-ai-harness ToolOutputLimits with strip_ansi=True and attacker-influenced tool output, including shell, file, fetched-page, or MCP-server output. Fixed in pydantic-ai-harness 0.70.0 or later; Pydantic AI v1 cannot use a harness newer than 0.4.0.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An untrusted tool-output boundary can exhaust the event loop before configured output limits apply, delaying concurrent requests and agent runs. The mitigation choice also has a Pydantic AI v1 compatibility constraint.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Pydantic AI product background belongs in ai-wiki; general agent-development adoption belongs in ai-dev-wiki. Retain tool-output trust, event-loop availability, version-compatibility, and upgrade-control implications in ai-security-wiki.

qualifying_findings.title: Junie CLI agent file tools can modify paths outside the project
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record with a JetBrains vendor security-issues reference; NVD records CVSS 7.5 High.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: JetBrains Junie CLI before 26.6.29; agent file tools could modify files outside the project directory.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The finding is a delegated-agent workspace-containment failure: project-scoped authority did not reliably constrain the file-system effects of an agent tool.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Junie product background and coding-agent workflow use belong upstream in ai-wiki and ai-dev-wiki respectively. Retain only the agent file-tool containment boundary, affected version, and patch implication locally.

qualifying_findings.title: Splunk AI Assistant has consent, retrieval, tenant-context, and feature-setting authorization flaws
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE records with the linked Splunk advisory. The four records describe one product-version boundary and related REST/assistant authorization defects.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Splunk AI Assistant versions below 2.0.0. CVE-2026-131302 permits unauthorized training-data-consent setting changes; CVE-2026-131303 exposes limited index/data-source information outside scope; CVE-2026-131304 accepts a client-controlled tenant identifier, enabling cross-tenant data access and misattribution; CVE-2026-131305 accepts client-controlled feature settings.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The group spans privacy-consent governance, retrieval authorization, tenant isolation, attribution integrity, and server-owned configuration boundaries in an AI assistant.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Splunk product background belongs in ai-wiki and general AI-assisted operational practice belongs in ai-dev-wiki. Retain the assistant-specific consent, retrieval authorization, tenant-context, and configuration-control failures in ai-security-wiki.

qualifying_findings.title: ServiceNow centrally remediated indirect prompt injection in an email-response AI agent
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record linked to a ServiceNow vendor security bulletin; NVD records CVSS 4.0 base score 7.1 High.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Email Response AI Agent in Now Assist for CSM. ServiceNow reports central remediation with no platform-version upgrade or hot fix and states it is not aware of malicious exploitation.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Untrusted email content can become indirect instructions at an autonomous response boundary. The vendor's centralized remediation is a concrete mitigation change but requires deployment owners to verify their service posture rather than wait for a local patch.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ServiceNow product context belongs in ai-wiki; general customer-service automation practice belongs in ai-dev-wiki. Retain the indirect-prompt-injection boundary, centrally deployed remediation, and exploitation-status qualifier locally.

qualifying_findings.title: Flyto2 Core fixes agent-workflow sandbox escapes, DNS-rebinding SSRF, and MCP recipe traversal
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Five NVD public CVE records with linked upstream GitHub security advisories, commits, and the v2.26.8 release. CVE-2026-77312 is recorded as CVSS 10.0 Critical; the remaining records range from Medium to High.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Flyto2 Core before 2.26.8. CVE-2026-77312 covers incomplete FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR file-write confinement; CVE-2026-77313 and CVE-2026-77316 cover DNS-rebinding bypasses of SSRF validation; CVE-2026-77314 covers MCP run_recipe path traversal beyond the bundled recipe directory; CVE-2026-77315 covers second-order SSRF through unvalidated pagination links.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A single AI-agent workflow runtime had failures across filesystem containment, outbound-network authority, MCP recipe selection, and server-provided continuation URLs. Upgrade is a release-gate and supply-chain control, while deployments should also reassess sandbox mounts, metadata-service reachability, and recipe/module policy.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Flyto product background belongs in ai-wiki and generic workflow development practice belongs in ai-dev-wiki. Retain the five security boundaries, affected release range, and deployment-control implications in ai-security-wiki.

upstream_routing_notes: Pydantic AI, Junie, Splunk, ServiceNow, and Flyto product/entity background routes to ai-wiki; this artifact retains only their security-specific implications.

General coding-agent, agent-runtime, and workflow adoption practices route to ai-dev-wiki; containment, authorization, privacy, prompt-injection, SSRF, and release-gate analysis stays in ai-security-wiki.

The Pydantic AI and Junie findings have existing local security lens coverage; new facts should be reconciled into their appropriate local leaves during normal ingest rather than duplicating broad product analysis.

confidence_notes: High confidence in the visible publication timestamps, CVE identifiers, affected-version statements, and linked-reference sets because NVD's public CVE API was queried during this run.

The Splunk CVEs are grouped because they share the same product version boundary and primary vendor advisory; preserve their distinct consent, retrieval, tenant, and configuration effects during synthesis.

The ServiceNow record explicitly says the remediation was centrally deployed and that no malicious exploitation is currently known; do not infer absence of future exploitation or an on-premises patch requirement.

The Flyto2 group is based on linked upstream advisories and v2.26.8 release evidence; confirm deployed package provenance and whether any locally enabled modules or MCP exposure affect practical reachability.
follow_up_actions: Upgrade pydantic-ai-harness to 0.70.0 or later where compatible; otherwise leave strip_ansi disabled and bound attacker-influenced tool output before event-loop processing.
Upgrade Junie CLI to 26.6.29 or later and independently verify tool operations cannot write beyond the approved project workspace.
Upgrade Splunk AI Assistant to 2.0.0 or later and test training-data consent, retrieval authorization, tenant-context binding, attribution, and feature-setting endpoints with low-privilege accounts.
Confirm the ServiceNow centrally deployed remediation status for Now Assist for CSM and keep untrusted email separated from executable agent instructions.

Upgrade Flyto2 Core to 2.26.8 or later; review sandbox mounts, file-write modules, DNS-rebinding-resistant outbound controls, metadata-service reachability, MCP recipe paths, and pagination follow behavior.
During normal raw-source ingest, retain only the security-specific local lens and route broad product/entity context upstream under federation rules.
blockers: No collection blocker. Before durable synthesis, confirm vendor fixed-release applicability for deployed Pydantic AI, Junie, Splunk, ServiceNow, and Flyto2 environments and avoid inferring exploitation beyond the source statements.

publication_safety.reason: The artifact preserves public advisory identifiers, affected boundaries, remediation references, routing, and defensive follow-up without reproducing exploit payloads or operational attack instructions.
